availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

// Fixed Phantom Writer script. These are inputs to the private simulator, not claimed results:
// every value in the log is decoded from the bytes that simulator actually received and sent.
public static class IncidentScript
{
    public const string ScenarioId = "phantom-writer";
    public const byte Unit = 5;
    public const ushort Register = 100;
    public const ushort InitialSetpoint = 650;
    public const ushort WrittenValue = 950;
    public const string ReaderClient = "HMI-01";
    public const string WriterClient = "MAINT-LAPTOP-07";
    public const ushort WriteTransactionId = 1111;
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 10, 31, 2, 13, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    public const string CaptureNote = "Simulated capture generated at server start from loopback exchanges with a private simulator. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; client labels are capture metadata.";

    public static readonly IncidentStep[] PhantomWriter = BuildSteps();

    private static IncidentStep[] BuildSteps()
    {
        var steps = new List<IncidentStep>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(i + 1), i * 5, 3, Register, 1));
        steps.Add(new(WriterClient, WriteTransactionId, 33, 6, Register, WrittenValue));
        int[] later = { 35, 40, 45, 50 };
        for (int i = 0; i < later.Length; i++) steps.Add(new(ReaderClient, (ushort)(8 + i), later[i], 3, Register, 1));
        return steps.ToArray();
    }
}

// Parameters of a Night Scanner capture. Production uses Default; the harness derives plans from seeds.
// These are inputs to the private gateway simulator, not claimed results.
public sealed record NightScannerPlan(int ScanUnits, byte RespondingUnit, ushort RespondingValue, int ScanStartSeconds, ushort ScanFirstTransactionId, string ScannerClient)
{
    public static readonly NightScannerPlan Default = new(10, 9, 1, 7, 301, "ENG-WS-13");
    private static readonly string[] Labels = { "ENG-WS-13", "VENDOR-RDP-2", "QA.LAPTOP_9" };

    public static NightScannerPlan FromSeed(ulong seed)
    {
        ulong state = seed;
        int Next(int min, int maxInclusive)
        {
            ulong z = state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15UL;
            z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9UL;
            z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBUL;
            z ^= z >> 31;
            return (int)(min + (long)(z % (ulong)(maxInclusive - min + 1)));
        }
        int units = Next(5, 12);
        var candidates = Enumerable.Range(1, units).Where(u => u != NightScannerScript.BoilerUnit).ToArray();
        return new(units, (byte)candidates[Next(0, candidates.Length - 1)], (ushort)Next(0, 65535), Next(1, 14), (ushort)Next(100, 60000), Labels[Next(0, Labels.Length - 1)]);
    }

    public void Validate()
    {

}

// The Night Scanner: HMI polling of unit 5 interleaved with an FC03 sweep of unit IDs 1..N. Reads only.
public static class NightScannerScript
{
    public const string ScenarioId = "night-scanner";
    public const byte BoilerUnit = 5;
    public const ushort Register = 100;
    public const ushort Setpoint = 650;
    public const string PollClient = "HMI-01";
    public const ushort ScanAddress = 0;
    public const int PollIntervalSeconds = 5;
    // Bounded like every Modbus exchange here, and within the 300 ms Modbus deadline, so startup stays fast.
    public static readonly TimeSpan ProbeDeadline = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100);
    public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 11, 1, 3, 12, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
    public const string CaptureNote = "Simulated capture generated at server start from loopback exchanges with a private gateway simulator. Modbus TCP frames carry no client identity; client labels are capture metadata. A request with no reply within 100 ms is logged as a timeout.";

    public static IncidentStep[] Build(NightScannerPlan plan)
    {
        plan.Validate();
        var timed = new List<(int Time, int Order, IncidentStep Step)>();
        int lastScan = plan.ScanStartSeconds + plan.ScanUnits - 1;
        ushort pollTx = 1;
        for (int t = 0; ; t += PollIntervalSeconds)
        {
            timed.Add((t, 0, new(PollClient, pollTx++, t, 3, Register, 1, BoilerUnit)));
            if (t > lastScan) break;
        }
        for (int k = 0; k < plan.ScanUnits; k++)
            timed.Add((plan.ScanStartSeconds + k, 1, new(plan.ScannerClient, (ushort)(plan.ScanFirstTransactionId + k), plan.ScanStartSeconds + k, 3, ScanAddress, 1, (byte)(k + 1))));
        // Interleave by simulated time; on a shared second the HMI poll comes first.
        return timed.OrderBy(x => x.Time).ThenBy(x => x.Order).Select(x => x.Step).ToArray();
    }

    public static Dictionary<int, Dictionary<int, Dictionary<int, ushort>>> Devices(NightScannerPlan plan) => new()
    {
        [BoilerUnit] = new() { [3] = new() { [Register] = Setpoint } },
        [plan.RespondingUnit] = new() { [3] = new() { [ScanAddress] = plan.RespondingValue } },
    };
}

// Startup-only component. It is the only code that encodes and sends FC06, and only to its own private,
// loopback-bound simulator, which is disposed before this method returns.
public static class IncidentLogGenerator
{
    private sealed class Recorder : IExchangeRecorder
    {
        private readonly object gate = new();
        private readonly List<SimulatorExchange> items = new();
        public void Record(SimulatorExchange exchange) { lock (gate) items.Add(exchange); }
        public SimulatorExchange[] Items { get { lock (gate) return items.ToArray(); } }
    }

    public static async Task<(TrafficLog Log, ushort FinalSetpoint)> GenerateAsync(CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var recorder = new Recorder();
        var script = IncidentScript.PhantomWriter;
        List<TrafficLogEntry> entries;
        await using (var simulator = new ModbusSimulator(IncidentScript.Unit, new() { [3] = new() { [IncidentScript.Register] = IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint } }, allowWrites: true, recorder: recorder))
            entries = await CaptureAsync(simulator, recorder, script, IncidentScript.Start, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(300), ct);

        // Validate the capture against the script: 650 before the write, an FC06 echo of 950, then 950.
        int writeIndex = Array.FindIndex(script, s => s.Function == 6);
        for (int i = 0; i < entries.Count; i++)
        {
            var e = entries[i];
            if (e.status != "response") throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has status {e.status}, expected a response");
            if (e.unit_id != IncidentScript.Unit || e.address != IncidentScript.Register || e.values.Length != 1)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has unexpected unit, address or values");
            ushort expected = i < writeIndex ? IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint : IncidentScript.WrittenValue;
            if (e.values[0] != expected) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} shows {e.values[0]}, expected {expected}");
            // An FC06 echo has the same MBAP header and PDU as its request, so the two frames are byte-identical.
            if (i == writeIndex && (e.function_code != 6 || e.frames.Count != 2 || e.frames[0].hex != e.frames[1].hex))
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture write is not an FC06 echo");
        }
        if (entries.Count(e => e.function_code == 6) != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture must contain exactly one write");
        ushort final = entries[^1].values[0];
        return (new TrafficLog(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, true, IncidentScript.CaptureNote, entries), final);
    }

    // Night Scanner: FC03 reads only, against a private read-only gateway that is disposed before this returns.
    public static async Task<TrafficLog> GenerateNightScannerAsync(NightScannerPlan plan, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var script = NightScannerScript.Build(plan);
        var recorder = new Recorder();
        List<TrafficLogEntry> entries;
        await using (var gateway = new ModbusSimulator(NightScannerScript.Devices(plan), recorder: recorder))
            entries = await CaptureAsync(gateway, recorder, script, NightScannerScript.Start, NightScannerScript.ProbeDeadline, ct);

        for (int i = 0; i < entries.Count; i++)
        {
            var e = entries[i];
            if (e.function_code != 3) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner entry {i + 1} is not FC03");
            string expected; ushort[] values = Array.Empty<ushort>(); int? code = null;
            if (e.client == NightScannerScript.PollClient)
            {
                if (e.unit_id != NightScannerScript.BoilerUnit || e.address != NightScannerScript.Register) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner poll {i + 1} has unexpected unit or address");
                expected = "response"; values = new[] { NightScannerScript.Setpoint };
            }
            else if (e.unit_id == plan.RespondingUnit) { expected = "response"; values = new[] { plan.RespondingValue }; }
            else if (e.unit_id == NightScannerScript.BoilerUnit) { expected = "exception"; code = 2; }
            else expected = "timeout";
            if (e.status != expected || !e.values.SequenceEqual(values) || e.exception_code != code)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner entry {i + 1} (unit {e.unit_id}) is {e.status}, expected {expected}");
        }
        var log = new TrafficLog(NightScannerScript.ScenarioId, true, NightScannerScript.CaptureNote, entries);
        var answer = Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log);
        if (answer == null || answer.client != plan.ScannerClient || answer.transaction_id != plan.ScanFirstTransactionId)
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Night Scanner capture does not show exactly one scanning client starting at the planned transaction");
        return log;
    }

    // Runs each step on its own loopback connection, strictly in order, and builds log entries from the bytes the
    // simulator recorded. A timeout is logged only when this client's deadline expired and the simulator sent nothing.
    private static async Task<List<TrafficLogEntry>> CaptureAsync(ModbusSimulator simulator, Recorder recorder, IReadOnlyList<IncidentStep> script,
                                                                  DateTimeOffset start, TimeSpan stepDeadline, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var ports = new int[script.Count];
        var timedOut = new bool[script.Count];
        if (script.Select(s => s.TransactionId).Distinct().Count() != script.Count) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident script transaction IDs must be unique");
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Count; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            var request = step.Function == 6
                ? ModbusCodec.EncodeWriteSingleRequest(step.TransactionId, step.Unit, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue)
                : ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest(step.TransactionId, step.Unit, step.Function, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue);
            using var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
            deadline.CancelAfter(stepDeadline);
            using var tcp = new TcpClient();
            await tcp.ConnectAsync(IPAddress.Loopback, simulator.Port, deadline.Token);
            ports[i] = ((IPEndPoint)tcp.Client.LocalEndPoint!).Port;
            using var stream = tcp.GetStream();
            await stream.WriteAsync(request, deadline.Token);
            try
            {
                var header = new byte[7];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(header, deadline.Token);
                int length = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(4));
                if (length is < 2 or > 254) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: invalid reply length {length}");
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(new byte[length - 1], deadline.Token);
                // The simulator records the exchange and then closes the connection, so end-of-stream means
                // this step's recording is complete and the steps stay strictly ordered.
                if (await stream.ReadAsync(new byte[1], deadline.Token) != 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: unexpected extra reply bytes");
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested) { timedOut[i] = true; }
        }

        // A silent simulator records on receipt; wait briefly in case that record is still in flight.
        for (int waited = 0; recorder.Items.Length < script.Count && waited < 1000; waited += 5) await Task.Delay(5, ct);
        var captured = recorder.Items;
        if (captured.Length != script.Count) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture has {captured.Length} exchanges, expected {script.Count}");
        var entries = new List<TrafficLogEntry>();
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Count; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            // The OS can reuse a client port within one capture, so match on the port and the transaction ID together.
            var matches = captured.Where(x => x.RemotePort == ports[i] && x.Received.Length >= 2 && BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(x.Received) == step.TransactionId).ToArray();
            if (matches.Length != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} does not match the connection opened for its step");
            var exchange = matches[0];
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request, out var request, out var requestError) || request == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} request did not decode: {requestError}");
            if (request.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || request.Header.UnitId != step.Unit || request.Function != step.Function)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} differs from the script");
            var frames = new List<DecodedFrame> { ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request) };
            string status; ushort[] values = Array.Empty<ushort>(); int? exceptionCode = null;
            if (exchange.Sent == null)
            {
                if (!timedOut[i]) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1}: the simulator sent nothing but the client did not time out");
                status = "timeout";
            }
            else
            {
                if (timedOut[i]) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1}: the client timed out but the simulator sent a reply");
                if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, out var response, out var responseError) || response == null)
                    throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} response did not decode: {responseError}");
                if (response.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || response.Header.UnitId != step.Unit || (response.Function & 0x7F) != step.Function)
                    throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} reply differs from the script");
                frames.Add(ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, request.Address));
                if (response.ExceptionCode.HasValue) { status = "exception"; exceptionCode = response.ExceptionCode.Value; }
                else { status = "response"; values = step.Function == 6 ? new[] { response.QuantityOrValue!.Value } : response.Registers; }
            }
            entries.Add(new(i + 1, start.AddSeconds(step.OffsetSeconds).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), step.Client,
                request.Header.TransactionId, request.Header.UnitId, request.Function, ModbusCodec.FunctionName(request.Function), request.Address!.Value, values, status, frames, exceptionCode));
        }
        return entries;
    }
}

            if (e.status != "response") throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has status {e.status}, expected a response");
            if (e.unit_id != IncidentScript.Unit || e.address != IncidentScript.Register || e.values.Length != 1)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} has unexpected unit, address or values");
            ushort expected = i < writeIndex ? IncidentScript.InitialSetpoint : IncidentScript.WrittenValue;
            if (e.values[0] != expected) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} shows {e.values[0]}, expected {expected}");
            // An FC06 echo has the same MBAP header and PDU as its request, so the two frames are byte-identical.
            if (i == writeIndex && (e.function_code != 6 || e.frames.Count != 2 || e.frames[0].hex != e.frames[1].hex))
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture write is not an FC06 echo");
        }
        if (entries.Count(e => e.function_code == 6) != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident capture must contain exactly one write");
        ushort final = entries[^1].values[0];
        return (new TrafficLog(IncidentScript.ScenarioId, true, IncidentScript.CaptureNote, entries), final);
    }

    // Night Scanner: FC03 reads only, against a private read-only gateway that is disposed before this returns.
    public static async Task<TrafficLog> GenerateNightScannerAsync(NightScannerPlan plan, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var script = NightScannerScript.Build(plan);
        var recorder = new Recorder();
        List<TrafficLogEntry> entries;
        await using (var gateway = new ModbusSimulator(NightScannerScript.Devices(plan), recorder: recorder))
            entries = await CaptureAsync(gateway, recorder, script, NightScannerScript.Start, NightScannerScript.ProbeDeadline, ct);

        for (int i = 0; i < entries.Count; i++)
        {
            var e = entries[i];
            if (e.function_code != 3) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner entry {i + 1} is not FC03");
            string expected; ushort[] values = Array.Empty<ushort>(); int? code = null;
            if (e.client == NightScannerScript.PollClient)
            {
                if (e.unit_id != NightScannerScript.BoilerUnit || e.address != NightScannerScript.Register) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner poll {i + 1} has unexpected unit or address");
                expected = "response"; values = new[] { NightScannerScript.Setpoint };
            }
            else if (e.unit_id == plan.RespondingUnit) { expected = "response"; values = new[] { plan.RespondingValue }; }
            else if (e.unit_id == NightScannerScript.BoilerUnit) { expected = "exception"; code = 2; }
            else expected = "timeout";
            if (e.status != expected || !e.values.SequenceEqual(values) || e.exception_code != code)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Night Scanner entry {i + 1} (unit {e.unit_id}) is {e.status}, expected {expected}");
        }
        var log = new TrafficLog(NightScannerScript.ScenarioId, true, NightScannerScript.CaptureNote, entries);
        var answer = Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log);
        if (answer == null || answer.client != plan.ScannerClient || answer.transaction_id != plan.ScanFirstTransactionId)
            throw new InvalidOperationException("Night Scanner capture does not show exactly one scanning client starting at the planned transaction");
        return log;
    }

    // Runs each step on its own loopback connection, strictly in order, and builds log entries from the bytes the
    // simulator recorded. A timeout is logged only when this client's deadline expired and the simulator sent nothing.
    private static async Task<List<TrafficLogEntry>> CaptureAsync(ModbusSimulator simulator, Recorder recorder, IReadOnlyList<IncidentStep> script,
                                                                  DateTimeOffset start, TimeSpan stepDeadline, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var ports = new int[script.Count];
        var timedOut = new bool[script.Count];
        if (script.Select(s => s.TransactionId).Distinct().Count() != script.Count) throw new InvalidOperationException("Incident script transaction IDs must be unique");
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Count; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            var request = step.Function == 6
                ? ModbusCodec.EncodeWriteSingleRequest(step.TransactionId, step.Unit, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue)
                : ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest(step.TransactionId, step.Unit, step.Function, step.Address, step.QuantityOrValue);
            using var deadline = CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct);
            deadline.CancelAfter(stepDeadline);
            using var tcp = new TcpClient();
            await tcp.ConnectAsync(IPAddress.Loopback, simulator.Port, deadline.Token);
            ports[i] = ((IPEndPoint)tcp.Client.LocalEndPoint!).Port;
            using var stream = tcp.GetStream();
            await stream.WriteAsync(request, deadline.Token);
            try
            {
                var header = new byte[7];
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(header, deadline.Token);
                int length = BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(header.AsSpan(4));
                if (length is < 2 or > 254) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: invalid reply length {length}");
                await stream.ReadExactlyAsync(new byte[length - 1], deadline.Token);
                // The simulator records the exchange and then closes the connection, so end-of-stream means
                // this step's recording is complete and the steps stay strictly ordered.
                if (await stream.ReadAsync(new byte[1], deadline.Token) != 0) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident step {step.TransactionId}: unexpected extra reply bytes");
            }
            catch (OperationCanceledException) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested) { timedOut[i] = true; }
        }

        // A silent simulator records on receipt; wait briefly in case that record is still in flight.
        for (int waited = 0; recorder.Items.Length < script.Count && waited < 1000; waited += 5) await Task.Delay(5, ct);
        var captured = recorder.Items;
        if (captured.Length != script.Count) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture has {captured.Length} exchanges, expected {script.Count}");
        var entries = new List<TrafficLogEntry>();
        for (int i = 0; i < script.Count; i++)
        {
            var step = script[i];
            // The OS can reuse a client port within one capture, so match on the port and the transaction ID together.
            var matches = captured.Where(x => x.RemotePort == ports[i] && x.Received.Length >= 2 && BinaryPrimitives.ReadUInt16BigEndian(x.Received) == step.TransactionId).ToArray();
            if (matches.Length != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} does not match the connection opened for its step");
            var exchange = matches[0];
            if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request, out var request, out var requestError) || request == null)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} request did not decode: {requestError}");
            if (request.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || request.Header.UnitId != step.Unit || request.Function != step.Function)
                throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} differs from the script");
            var frames = new List<DecodedFrame> { ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Received, FrameDirection.Request) };
            string status; ushort[] values = Array.Empty<ushort>(); int? exceptionCode = null;
            if (exchange.Sent == null)
            {
                if (!timedOut[i]) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1}: the simulator sent nothing but the client did not time out");
                status = "timeout";
            }
            else
            {
                if (timedOut[i]) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1}: the client timed out but the simulator sent a reply");
                if (!ModbusCodec.TryParse(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, out var response, out var responseError) || response == null)
                    throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} response did not decode: {responseError}");
                if (response.Header.TransactionId != step.TransactionId || response.Header.UnitId != step.Unit || (response.Function & 0x7F) != step.Function)
                    throw new InvalidOperationException($"Incident capture entry {i + 1} reply differs from the script");
                frames.Add(ModbusCodec.Decode(exchange.Sent, FrameDirection.Response, request.Address));
                if (response.ExceptionCode.HasValue) { status = "exception"; exceptionCode = response.ExceptionCode.Value; }
                else { status = "response"; values = step.Function == 6 ? new[] { response.QuantityOrValue!.Value } : response.Registers; }
            }
            entries.Add(new(i + 1, start.AddSeconds(step.OffsetSeconds).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss'Z'", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture), step.Client,
                request.Header.TransactionId, request.Header.UnitId, request.Function, ModbusCodec.FunctionName(request.Function), request.Address!.Value, values, status, frames, exceptionCode));
        }
        return entries;
    }
}

// Progressive training hints, kept client-side: none for the first 2 unverified answers,
// hint 1 from the 3rd, hint 2 from the 4th. Hidden once an answer is verified. They never name the row.
// The hint text is case-specific and comes from the scenario's `incident` field.
const hintThreshold = 3;

function answerHints(scenarioId) {
  const hints = scenarios.find((item) => item.id === scenarioId)?.incident?.hints;
  return Array.isArray(hints) ? hints : [];
}

function renderAnswerHints(scenarioId) {
  const hints = answerHints(scenarioId);
  const attempts = answerHistory.get(scenarioId) || [];
  const wrong = attempts.filter((entry) => entry.verified !== true).length;
  const shown = attempts.some((entry) => entry.verified === true) ? 0 : Math.max(0, Math.min(hints.length, wrong - hintThreshold + 1));
  const list = $('answer-hint-list');
  list.replaceChildren();
  hints.slice(0, shown).forEach((hint, index) => addText(list, 'li', `Training hint ${index + 1}: ${hint}`));
  $('answer-hints').hidden = shown === 0;
  return shown;
}

function renderAnswer(result) {
  $('answer-result').hidden = false;
  const ok = result.verified === true;
  $('answer-status').textContent = ok ? 'Status: answer verified' : 'Status: answer not verified';
  $('answer-status').dataset.state = ok ? 'success' : 'error';
  for (const key of ['observations', 'possible_causes', 'training_hints', 'next_steps']) fillList($(`answer-${key}`), result[key]);
  const mitigations = Array.isArray(result.mitigations) ? result.mitigations : [];
  $('mitigations-section').hidden = mitigations.length === 0;
  fillList($('answer-mitigations'), mitigations);
  $('answer-verified').textContent = ok ? 'Verified by the simulated capture: this transaction ID and client label match the evidence for this case.' : 'Not verified by the simulated capture.';
  $('answer-verified').parentElement.dataset.state = ok ? 'success' : '';
  $('answer-explanation').textContent = text(result.explanation, 'No explanation returned.');
  $('answer-explanation-source').textContent = sourceText(result.explanation_source);
}

function renderAnswerHistory() {
  const list = $('answer-history');
  list.replaceChildren();
  const scenario = currentScenario();
  const attempts = scenario ? (answerHistory.get(scenario.id) || []) : [];
  $('answer-history-title').hidden = attempts.length === 0;
  attempts.forEach((entry, index) => {
    const item = document.createElement('li');
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    addText(details, 'summary', `Answer ${index + 1} · transaction ${text(entry.answer?.transaction_id)} · client ${text(entry.answer?.client)} · ${entry.verified === true ? 'Verified by the simulated capture.' : 'Not verified by the simulated capture.'}`);
    const body = document.createElement('div');
    body.className = 'history-detail';
    for (const [key, label] of [...categories, ['mitigations', 'Next steps · real-world guidance, not verified by this simulation']]) {
      if (key === 'mitigations' && !(entry.mitigations || []).length) continue;
      addText(body, 'h3', label);
      const ul = document.createElement('ul');
      fillList(ul, entry[key]);
      body.append(ul);
    }
    addText(body, 'h3', `Explanation · ${sourceText(entry.explanation_source)}`);
    addText(body, 'p', text(entry.explanation, 'No explanation returned.'));
    details.append(body);
    item.append(details);
    list.append(item);
  });
  if (attempts.length) {
    $('print-report').disabled = false;
    $('history-empty').hidden = true;
  }
}

$('answer-form').addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (answering) return;
  if (!$('answer-form').reportValidity()) return;
  const scenario = currentScenario();
  if (!scenario || scenario.category !== 'security') return;
  const request = { scenario_id: scenario.id, transaction_id: Number($('answer-transaction').value), client: $('answer-client').value.trim() };
  answering = true;
  $('answer-fields').disabled = true;
  // Not `disabled`: a disabled button would drop keyboard focus while the result is announced.
  $('submit-answer').setAttribute('aria-disabled', 'true');
  $('test-message').dataset.state = '';
  $('test-message').textContent = 'Checking your answer against the simulated capture…';
  try {
    const result = await api('/api/incident/answer', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(request) });
    if (!result.answer) result.answer = request;
    const attempts = answerHistory.get(scenario.id) || [];
    const hintsBefore = renderAnswerHints(scenario.id);
    attempts.push(result);
    answerHistory.set(scenario.id, attempts);
    if (result.verified === true) verifiedTransaction.set(scenario.id, result.answer.transaction_id);
    renderAnswer(result);
    if (incidentLogs.has(scenario.id)) renderLog(scenario.id);
    renderAnswerHistory();
    const hintsAfter = renderAnswerHints(scenario.id);
    $('test-message').textContent = result.verified === true
      ? `Answer verified by the simulated capture. The matching log row is now marked "${flagLabel(scenario.id).replace(/^⚠\s*/, '')}".`
      : `Answer not verified by the simulated capture. Review the log and try again.${hintsAfter > hintsBefore ? ` Training hint ${hintsAfter}: ${answerHints(scenario.id)[hintsAfter - 1]}` : ''}`;
  } catch (error) {
    $('test-message').textContent = `Answer failed: ${error.message}`;
    $('test-message').dataset.state = 'error';
  } finally {
    answering = false;
    $('answer-fields').disabled = false;
    $('submit-answer').removeAttribute('aria-disabled');
  }
});

$('scenario').addEventListener('change', selectScenario);
$('scale').addEventListener('input', validateScale);
for (const field of Object.keys(fieldRules)) $(field).addEventListener('input', () => setInvalid(field, false));

// Guided tour banner for first-time visitors. Dismissal is remembered in localStorage when available.
const tourKey = 'ghostwire.tourDismissed';
const tourScenario = 'unit-id';
function tourDismissed() {
  try { return localStorage.getItem(tourKey) === '1'; } catch { return false; }
}

using (var response = await client.GetAsync("/api/incident/unit-id/log")) Check(response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound, "log 404 for a troubleshooting case");
using (var response = await client.GetAsync("/api/incident/night-scanner/log")) Check(response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.OK, "Night Scanner log is served");
using (var response = await client.GetAsync("/api/incident/NIGHT-SCANNER/log")) Check(response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound, "log ids match exactly");
using (var response = await client.GetAsync("/api/incident/../log")) Check(response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound, "log 404 for a path-traversal id");
using (var response = await client.GetAsync("/api/incident/%2E%2E%2Fscenarios/log")) Check(response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.NotFound, "log 404 for an encoded traversal id");

// Incident answer endpoint.
async Task<(HttpStatusCode Status, JsonElement Body)> Answer(HttpContent content)
{
    using var response = await client.PostAsync("/api/incident/answer", content);
    var body = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();
    return (response.StatusCode, JsonDocument.Parse(body).RootElement.Clone());
}
HttpContent AnswerJson(int tx, string label) => JsonContent.Create(new { scenario_id = "phantom-writer", transaction_id = tx, client = label });
var correct = await Answer(AnswerJson(1111, "MAINT-LAPTOP-07"));

Run the harness after every task from the repository root: `tools/dotnet run --project csharp/GhostWire.Tests/GhostWire.Tests.csproj`. A task is done only when the harness prints `All GhostWire protocol and HTTP checks passed.` No NuGet packages. No commits.

- [x] 5.1 Example checks for the scenario, learner read, FC06 rejection, default log, determinism, answers and 404s; update the scenario count to 5.
  - _Requirements: 6.1, 1.3, 1.4, 2.8, 3.3, 3.6_
- [x] 5.2 Property P-f: Night Scanner capture over seeded plans (≥ 48 cases, batches of 8)
  - _Requirements: 6.2, 6.3, 6.4_

- [x] 6. Frontend
  - Status column with text for response, timeout and exception (decoded code and name); "None" for empty values; frames row spans 10 columns.
  - Case-specific task text, hints and flag label from `scenario.incident`.
  - _Requirements: 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7_

- [x] 7. Documentation
  - README case table to five cases; `docs/judge-quick-start.md` Night Scanner steps; `csharp/README.md` API and generation notes; `docs/verification.md` with observed harness values.
  - _Requirements: 7.1, 7.2, 7.3_

| `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateAsync` | Unchanged entry point for Phantom Writer | The connection, recording and decoding loop moves into a shared `CaptureAsync` that also records `timeout` and `exception` entries. Each case keeps its own validation. | | `TrafficLogEntry` | Same entry shape | Additive `exception_code` (int or null). `status` can now be `timeout` or `exception`. | | `TrainingService.IncidentLog(id)` and `GET /api/incident/{id}/log` | Same route | Logs stored in a dictionary keyed by the fixed security case IDs. | | `Diagnosis.ForAnswer` and `POST /api/incident/answer` | Same route and request shape | Dispatches on `log.scenario_id`. New `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log)` gives the correct entry per case and drives the existing redaction. Mitigations chosen per case. | | Frontend log table, answer form, progressive hints, row flag | Same components | New Status column. Task text, hints and flag label come from the scenario's `incident` field instead of Phantom Writer constants. | Device choice: the gateway routes **the same boiler controller at unit 5** as Phantom Writer, here with its normal setpoint 650 (a different simulated night, no write). Reusing the device keeps the documentation familiar and lets the initial read look normal, which is the point of the case: the process value is fine and the evidence is in the network capture. Design choices that resolve tensions in the brief: | Tension | Decision | Reason | |---|---|---| | "Same bounded timeout as elsewhere" vs. "make timeouts in the generator short" | Every Night Scanner exchange uses a 100 ms probe deadline, bounded by the same cancellation-token= and within the 300 ms Modbus deadline. Learner reads keep 300 ms. The capture note states the 100 ms value. | With the default plan, 8 sweep requests get no reply. At 300 ms that adds 2.4 s to every start and to every property case; at 100 ms it adds 0.8 s. Loopback replies arrive in about 1 ms, so 100 ms leaves a wide margin. | | A timeout must be real, not scripted | An entry is `timeout` only when the generator's deadline expired **and** the simulator recorder reports `Sent == null` for that connection. Any disagreement fails startup. | The log status is evidence from both ends of the exchange, not a constant. | | "Exactly one correct answer" must not come from script constants | `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry` derives the scanning client from the log (the only client addressing ≥ 3 distinct unit IDs) and takes its first entry. The generator checks that this equals the plan. | The verified rule depends only on evidence, like Phantom Writer's "values read from log entries". | | A property "for any seed" vs. a deterministic production log | `NightScannerPlan.Default` is fixed. `NightScannerPlan.FromSeed(seed)` derives a plan for tests from a SplitMix64 sequence. Both go through the same generator and validation. | Production stays deterministic (Req. 2.8); the property covers many plans. | | Hints are case-specific | Hints, task text and the flag label move to an additive `incident` object in `GET /api/scenarios`. | Avoids hard-coding scenario IDs in `app.js` and keeps Phantom Writer's text unchanged. | | Answer redaction could hint at the answer | Keep Phantom Writer's rule: redact `log_entry.client` only when the submitted transaction is the answer entry and the answer is not verified. | Same behavior across security cases. The row itself already shows the label. | Out of scope: writes of any kind in the Night Scanner, Modbus gateway exception codes 0A/0B (the simulator stays silent, as documented in `modbus-protocol.md`), multiple scans per capture, sub-second timestamps. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph "Startup (before HTTP)" P[NightScannerPlan.Default] --> B[NightScannerScript.Build] B -- "IncidentStep[] (FC03 only)" --> C[IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync] C -- "loopback TCP, 100 ms per request" --> G[(Private gateway simulator
unit 5 + unit U, read-only)] G -- "recorder: received / sent bytes" --> C C --> V[Night Scanner validation
+ Diagnosis.AnswerEntry] V --> L[TrafficLog night-scanner] end L --> T[TrainingService] T --> LG[(Learner-facing gateway simulator
same device map, read-only)] UI[app.js] -- "GET /api/incident/night-scanner/log
POST /api/incident/answer
POST /api/test" --> T ``` Startup: the `TrainingService` constructor creates the troubleshooting simulators, generates the Phantom Writer log, then the Night Scanner log, all under one 5 s deadline, then creates the learner-facing `night-scanner` gateway simulator. The private gateway is disposed when `GenerateNightScannerAsync` returns. `GhostWireHost.Create` already resolves `TrainingService` eagerly, so a failure stops startup. Note: To continue, use offset 50.

The old constructor delegates to it. Unknown unit IDs stay silent, as today. | | `IncidentStep` | Every HMI poll and scan request | Optional `Unit` parameter, default `IncidentScript.Unit` (5), so the Phantom Writer script is unchanged. | | `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateAsync` | Unchanged entry point for Phantom Writer | The connection, recording and decoding loop moves into a shared `CaptureAsync` that also records `timeout` and `exception` entries. Each case keeps its own validation. | | `TrafficLogEntry` | Same entry shape | Additive `exception_code` (int or null). `status` can now be `timeout` or `exception`. | | `TrainingService.IncidentLog(id)` and `GET /api/incident/{id}/log` | Same route | Logs stored in a dictionary keyed by the fixed security case IDs. | | `Diagnosis.ForAnswer` and `POST /api/incident/answer` | Same route and request shape | Dispatches on `log.scenario_id`. New `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log)` gives the correct entry per case and drives the existing redaction. Mitigations chosen per case. | | Frontend log table, answer form, progressive hints, row flag | Same components | New Status column. Task text, hints and flag label come from the scenario's `incident` field instead of Phantom Writer constants. | Device choice: the gateway routes **the same boiler controller at unit 5** as Phantom Writer, here with its normal setpoint 650 (a different simulated night, no write). Reusing the device keeps the documentation familiar and lets the initial read look normal, which is the point of the case: the process value is fine and the evidence is in the network capture. Design choices that resolve tensions in the brief: | Tension | Decision | Reason | |---|---|---| | "Same bounded timeout as elsewhere" vs. "make timeouts in the generator short" | Every Night Scanner exchange uses a 100 ms probe deadline, bounded by the same cancellation-token= and within the 300 ms Modbus deadline. Learner reads keep 300 ms. The capture note states the 100 ms value. | With the default plan, 8 sweep requests get no reply. At 300 ms that adds 2.4 s to every start and to every property case; at 100 ms it adds 0.8 s. Loopback replies arrive in about 1 ms, so 100 ms leaves a wide margin. | | A timeout must be real, not scripted | An entry is `timeout` only when the generator's deadline expired **and** the simulator recorder reports `Sent == null` for that connection. Any disagreement fails startup. | The log status is evidence from both ends of the exchange, not a constant. | | "Exactly one correct answer" must not come from script constants | `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry` derives the scanning client from the log (the only client addressing ≥ 3 distinct unit IDs) and takes its first entry. The generator checks that this equals the plan. | The verified rule depends only on evidence, like Phantom Writer's "values read from log entries". | | A property "for any seed" vs. a deterministic production log | `NightScannerPlan.Default` is fixed. `NightScannerPlan.FromSeed(seed)` derives a plan for tests from a SplitMix64 sequence. Both go through the same generator and validation. | Production stays deterministic (Req. 2.8); the property covers many plans. | | Hints are case-specific | Hints, task text and the flag label move to an additive `incident` object in `GET /api/scenarios`. | Avoids hard-coding scenario IDs in `app.js` and keeps Phantom Writer's text unchanged. | | Answer redaction could hint at the answer | Keep Phantom Writer's rule: redact `log_entry.client` only when the submitted transaction is the answer entry and the answer is not verified. | Same behavior across security cases. The row itself already shows the label. | Out of scope: writes of any kind in the Night Scanner, Modbus gateway exception codes 0A/0B (the simulator stays silent, as documented in `modbus-protocol.md`), multiple scans per capture, sub-second timestamps. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph "Startup (before HTTP)" P[NightScannerPlan.Default] --> B[NightScannerScript.Build] B -- "IncidentStep[] (FC03 only)" --> C[IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync] C -- "loopback TCP, 100 ms per request" --> G[(Private gateway simulator
unit 5 + unit U, read-only)] G -- "recorder: received / sent bytes" --> C C --> V[Night Scanner validation
+ Diagnosis.AnswerEntry] V --> L[TrafficLog night-scanner] end L --> T[TrainingService] T --> LG[(Learner-facing gateway simulator
same device map, read-only)] UI[app.js] -- "GET /api/incident/night-scanner/log
POST /api/incident/answer
POST /api/test" --> T ``` Startup: the `TrainingService` constructor creates the troubleshooting simulators, generates the Phantom Writer log, then the Night Scanner log, all under one 5 s deadline, then creates the learner-facing `night-scanner` gateway simulator. The private gateway is disposed when `GenerateNightScannerAsync` returns. `GhostWireHost.Create` already resolves `TrainingService` eagerly, so a failure stops startup. ## Components and Interfaces ### `ModbusSimulator` (changed, `Modbus.cs`) ```csharp public ModbusSimulator(int unit, Dictionary> registers, bool allowWrites = false, IExchangeRecorder? recorder = null) : this(new Dictionary>> { [unit] = registers }, allowWrites, recorder) { } public ModbusSimulator(Dictionary>> devices, bool allowWrites = false, IExchangeRecorder? recorder = null); ``` `ServeAsync` looks up `devices[header[6]]`. A missing unit is recorded with `Sent = null` and kept silent, exactly as the single-unit mismatch today. All other request handling is unchanged. ### `IncidentStep`, `TrafficLogEntry` (changed, `Incident.cs`) ```csharp public sealed record IncidentStep(string Client, ushort TransactionId, int OffsetSeconds, byte Function, ushort Address, ushort QuantityOrValue, byte Unit = IncidentScript.Unit); public sealed record TrafficLogEntry(..., string status, IReadOnlyList frames, int? exception_code = null); ``` ### `IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync` (extracted) ```csharp private static async Task> CaptureAsync(ModbusSimulator simulator, Recorder recorder, IReadOnlyList script, DateTimeOffset start, TimeSpan stepDeadline, CancellationToken= step, strictly in order: open a new `TcpClient` to `IPAddress.Loopback` and the simulator's port, remember the local port, write the encoded request, then read the 7-byte header and PDU and wait for end of stream under `stepDeadline`. If that deadline expires (and `ct` has not), the step's client observation is `timeout`. Connect and write are also under the deadline but are not caught: a failure there is a startup error. After all steps, wait (bounded by `ct`, at most 1 s) until the recorder holds one exchange per step, then match exchanges to steps by remote port **and** transaction ID (script transaction IDs must be unique). Port alone is not enough: property P-f found that Windows can reuse a client port within one capture when 8 captures run at once (seed 987654321, case 25). For each step: - Recorder `Sent == null` and client observed `timeout` → `status: "timeout"`, frames `[request]`, `values: []`. - Recorder `Sent != null` and client observed a reply → decode the response. `fc & 0x80` → `status: "exception"`, `exception_code`, `values: []`. Otherwise `status: "response"`, values from the decoded registers (FC06: the echoed value). - Any other combination, a request that does not decode, or a transaction ID, unit ID or function mismatch with the step → `InvalidOperationException`. `unit_id`, `function_code`, `address` and `values` come from the decoded captured bytes. Phantom Writer calls `CaptureAsync` with its private write-enabled simulator and a 300 ms step deadline, then runs its existing validation (all 12 `response`, 650 → 950, FC06 echo where request and response hex are equal). ### `NightScannerPlan` and `NightScannerScript` (new, `Incident.cs`) ```csharp public sealed record NightScannerPlan(int ScanUnits, byte RespondingUnit, ushort RespondingValue, int ScanStartSeconds, ushort ScanFirstTransactionId, string ScannerClient) { public static readonly NightScannerPlan Default = new(10, 9, 1, 7, 301, "ENG-WS-13"); public static NightScannerPlan FromSeed(ulong seed); // tests only } public static class NightScannerScript { public const string ScenarioId = "night-scanner"; public const byte BoilerUnit = 5; public const ushort Register = 100; public const ushort Setpoint = 650; public const string PollClient = "HMI-01"; public const ushort ScanAddress = 0; public static readonly TimeSpan ProbeDeadline = TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100); public static readonly DateTimeOffset Start = new(2026, 11, 1, 3, 12, 0, TimeSpan.Zero); public static IncidentStep[] Build(NightScannerPlan plan); public static Dictionary>> Devices(NightScannerPlan plan); } ``` Plan constraints (checked by a `Validate` method that throws): 5 ≤ `ScanUnits` ≤ 12; 1 ≤ `RespondingUnit` ≤ `ScanUnits` and ≠ 5; 1 ≤ `ScanStartSeconds` ≤ 30; first scan transaction ID ≥ 100 and the scan range stays ≤ 65535; client label matches `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,32}` and differs from `HMI-01`. `FromSeed`: SplitMix64 over the seed picks `ScanUnits` 5–12, `RespondingUnit` from 1–N without 5, `RespondingValue` 0–65535, `ScanStartSeconds` 1–14, first transaction ID 100–60000, and the label from {`ENG-WS-13`, `VENDOR-RDP-2`, `QA.LAPTOP_9`}. `Build`: HMI polls at 0, 5, 10, … simulated seconds, transaction IDs 1, 2, 3, …, until the poll after the last scan request. Scan request k (k = 0 … N−1) at `ScanStartSeconds + k`, unit k+1, transaction `ScanFirstTransactionId + k`. Merged by time, HMI first on ties. All steps are FC03, quantity 1. Default plan, as inputs (the log values are whatever the simulator returns): scan of units 1–10 at 03:12:07–03:12:16 by `ENG-WS-13`, transactions 301–310; HMI polls at 03:12:00, :05, :10, :15, :20, transactions 1–5; 15 entries in total. `Devices(plan)`: `{ 5: { 3: { 100: 650 } }, U: { 3: { 0: RespondingValue } } }`. ### `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateNightScannerAsync` (new) ```csharp public static Task GenerateNightScannerAsync(NightScannerPlan plan, CancellationToken= Validate the plan; build the script. 2. Create a private, read-only gateway simulator with `Devices(plan)` and a recorder. It is never stored outside this method. 3. `CaptureAsync(..., NightScannerScript.ProbeDeadline, ct)`, then dispose the simulator. 4. + Diagnosis.AnswerEntry] V --> L[TrafficLog night-scanner] end L --> T[TrainingService] T --> LG[(Learner-facing gateway simulator
same device map, read-only)] UI[app.js] -- "GET /api/incident/night-scanner/log

# Design Document: night-scanner ## Overview The Night Scanner is the second `security` case. It reuses the Phantom Writer pipeline end to end: | Phantom Writer piece | Reused as | Generalisation needed | |---|---|---| | `ModbusSimulator(unit, registers, allowWrites, recorder)` | Private and learner-facing gateway simulators | New constructor that takes a map of unit ID → register maps. The old constructor delegates to it. Unknown unit IDs stay silent, as today. | | `IncidentStep` | Every HMI poll and scan request | Optional `Unit` parameter, default `IncidentScript.Unit` (5), so the Phantom Writer script is unchanged. | | `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateAsync` | Unchanged entry point for Phantom Writer | The connection, recording and decoding loop moves into a shared `CaptureAsync` that also records `timeout` and `exception` entries. Each case keeps its own validation. | | `TrafficLogEntry` | Same entry shape | Additive `exception_code` (int or null). `status` can now be `timeout` or `exception`. | | `TrainingService.IncidentLog(id)` and `GET /api/incident/{id}/log` | Same route | Logs stored in a dictionary keyed by the fixed security case IDs. | | `Diagnosis.ForAnswer` and `POST /api/incident/answer` | Same route and request shape | Dispatches on `log.scenario_id`. New `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log)` gives the correct entry per case and drives the existing redaction. Mitigations chosen per case. | | Frontend log table, answer form, progressive hints, row flag | Same components | New Status column. Task text, hints and flag label come from the scenario's `incident` field instead of Phantom Writer constants. | Device choice: the gateway routes **the same boiler controller at unit 5** as Phantom Writer, here with its normal setpoint 650 (a different simulated night, no write). Reusing the device keeps the documentation familiar and lets the initial read look normal, which is the point of the case: the process value is fine and the evidence is in the network capture. Design choices that resolve tensions in the brief: | Tension | Decision | Reason | |---|---|---| | "Same bounded timeout as elsewhere" vs. "make timeouts in the generator short" | Every Night Scanner exchange uses a 100 ms probe deadline, bounded by the same cancellation-token= and within the 300 ms Modbus deadline. Learner reads keep 300 ms. The capture note states the 100 ms value. | With the default plan, 8 sweep requests get no reply. At 300 ms that adds 2.4 s to every start and to every property case; at 100 ms it adds 0.8 s. Loopback replies arrive in about 1 ms, so 100 ms leaves a wide margin. | | A timeout must be real, not scripted | An entry is `timeout` only when the generator's deadline expired **and** the simulator recorder reports `Sent == null` for that connection. Any disagreement fails startup. | The log status is evidence from both ends of the exchange, not a constant. | | "Exactly one correct answer" must not come from script constants | `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry` derives the scanning client from the log (the only client addressing ≥ 3 distinct unit IDs) and takes its first entry. The generator checks that this equals the plan. | The verified rule depends only on evidence, like Phantom Writer's "values read from log entries". | | A property "for any seed" vs. a deterministic production log | `NightScannerPlan.Default` is fixed. `NightScannerPlan.FromSeed(seed)` derives a plan for tests from a SplitMix64 sequence. Both go through the same generator and validation. | Production stays deterministic (Req. 2.8); the property covers many plans. | | Hints are case-specific | Hints, task text and the flag label move to an additive `incident` object in `GET /api/scenarios`. | Avoids hard-coding scenario IDs in `app.js` and keeps Phantom Writer's text unchanged. | | Answer redaction could hint at the answer | ~~Keep Phantom Writer's rule: redact `log_entry.client` only when the submitted transaction is the answer entry.~~ Revised after the session 10 security review: the redaction and the "client label differs" wording marked the answer row (an answer oracle against Req. 3.6). Every unverified answer in both security cases now gets one identical reply with `log_entry: null`; only the echoed `answer` differs. Progressive hints stay client-side and generic. | The reply must not depend on which part of the pair was wrong. The harness checks this byte for byte for every log entry of both cases. | | A step deadline can expire during connect or write | `CaptureAsync` catches step-deadline cancellation around connect and write and rethrows `InvalidOperationException` naming the step and its deadline. The "5 s startup deadline" message is kept only for cancellation of the outer token. | The startup error names the real cause. | Out of scope: writes of any kind in the Night Scanner, Modbus gateway exception codes 0A/0B (the simulator stays silent, as documented in `modbus-protocol.md`), multiple scans per capture, sub-second timestamps. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph "Startup (before HTTP)" P[NightScannerPlan.Default] --> B[NightScannerScript.Build] B -- "IncidentStep[] (FC03 only)" --> C[IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync] C -- "loopback TCP, 100 ms per request" --> G[(Private gateway simulator
unit 5 + unit U, read-only)] G -- "recorder: received / sent bytes" --> C C --> V[Night Scanner validation
+ Diagnosis.AnswerEntry] V --> L[TrafficLog night-scanner] end L --> T[TrainingService] T --> LG[(Learner-facing gateway simulator
same device map, read-only)] UI[app.js] -- "GET /api/incident/night-scanner/log
POST /api/incident/answer
POST /api/test" --> T ``` Startup: the `TrainingService` constructor creates the troubleshooting simulators, generates the Phantom Writer log, then the Night Scanner log, all under one 5 s deadline, then creates the learner-facing `night-scanner` gateway simulator. A missing unit is recorded with `Sent = null` and kept silent, exactly as the single-unit mismatch today. All other request handling is unchanged. ### `IncidentStep`, `TrafficLogEntry` (changed, `Incident.cs`) ```csharp public sealed record IncidentStep(string Client, ushort TransactionId, int OffsetSeconds, byte Function, ushort Address, ushort QuantityOrValue, byte Unit = IncidentScript.Unit); public sealed record TrafficLogEntry(..., string status, IReadOnlyList frames, int? exception_code = null); ``` ### `IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync` (extracted) ```csharp private static async Task> CaptureAsync(ModbusSimulator simulator, Recorder recorder, IReadOnlyList script, DateTimeOffset start, TimeSpan stepDeadline, CancellationToken= step, strictly in order: open a new `TcpClient` to `IPAddress.Loopback` and the simulator's port, remember the local port, write the encoded request, then read the 7-byte header and PDU and wait for end of stream under `stepDeadline`. A read of unit 1 times out and a read of unit 9 returns a response on the learner-facing gateway. - Raw FC06 to the learner-facing gateway returns `86 01`; register 100 still reads 650. - Default log: 15 entries; 5 from `HMI-01` (all response 650, unit 5); 10 from `ENG-WS-13` with unit IDs 1–10, transactions 301–310; 8 timeouts with one request frame each, unit 5 exception 02, unit 9 response; every frame re-decodes to its entry; identical JSON across two `TrainingService` instances; no FC06 entries. - Answers: `301` / `ENG-WS-13` verifies with four mitigations and observations citing the label, `1 to 10`, 301, 310, `8 timeout`, unit 9. Property P-f **Night Scanner capture** (seeded, printed base seed, per-property seed as in the harness): 48 cases in batches of 8. For each case, `plan = NightScannerPlan.FromSeed(rng.Next())`, `log = await GenerateNightScannerAsync(plan, 5 s)`. Assert: scanning client's unit IDs strictly increase and equal 1…N; exactly one scan entry is `response` and it is unit U; unit 5's scan entry is `exception` 02; all other scan entries are `timeout` with exactly one frame; transaction IDs are unique; and over all pairs (transaction ID from the log × client label from the log, plus each transaction with a lower-cased label) exactly one pair verifies through `Diagnosis.ForAnswer`, and it is (first scan transaction, scanner label). Expected runtime: about 1 s per batch. Browser check (temporary script outside the repository, deleted afterwards): case listed under "Security incidents"; log shows the scan with Status text; three wrong answers show hint 1; the correct answer verifies and flags the row; no console errors; no horizontal overflow at 360 px. ## Safety Review Checklist - No new input selects a host, port or URL. `night-scanner` is a fixed dictionary key. - The Night Scanner generator encodes only FC03 (`ModbusCodec.EncodeReadRequest` throws for anything else). - Both gateway simulators bind loopback, use `allowWrites: false` and answer FC06 with exception 01. - The private gateway is disposed before the server serves HTTP. - Every status, value and frame in the log is decoded from captured bytes and cross-checked with the recorder. - Mitigations are labeled real-world guidance not verified by this simulation.

# Design Document: night-scanner ## Overview The Night Scanner is the second `security` case. It reuses the Phantom Writer pipeline end to end: | Phantom Writer piece | Reused as | Generalisation needed | |---|---|---| | `ModbusSimulator(unit, registers, allowWrites, recorder)` | Private and learner-facing gateway simulators | New constructor that takes a map of unit ID → register maps. The old constructor delegates to it. Unknown unit IDs stay silent, as today. | | `IncidentStep` | Every HMI poll and scan request | Optional `Unit` parameter, default `IncidentScript.Unit` (5), so the Phantom Writer script is unchanged. | | `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateAsync` | Unchanged entry point for Phantom Writer | The connection, recording and decoding loop moves into a shared `CaptureAsync` that also records `timeout` and `exception` entries. Each case keeps its own validation. | | `TrafficLogEntry` | Same entry shape | Additive `exception_code` (int or null). `status` can now be `timeout` or `exception`. | | `TrainingService.IncidentLog(id)` and `GET /api/incident/{id}/log` | Same route | Logs stored in a dictionary keyed by the fixed security case IDs. | | `Diagnosis.ForAnswer` and `POST /api/incident/answer` | Same route and request shape | Dispatches on `log.scenario_id`. New `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry(log)` gives the correct entry per case. Every unverified answer returns one identical reply without a log entry. Mitigations chosen per case. | | Frontend log table, answer form, progressive hints, row flag | Same components | New Status column. Task text, hints and flag label come from the scenario's `incident` field instead of Phantom Writer constants. | Device choice: the gateway routes **the same boiler controller at unit 5** as Phantom Writer, here with its normal setpoint 650 (a different simulated night, no write). Reusing the device keeps the documentation familiar and lets the initial read look normal, which is the point of the case: the process value is fine and the evidence is in the network capture. Design choices that resolve tensions in the brief: | Tension | Decision | Reason | |---|---|---| | "Same bounded timeout as elsewhere" vs. "make timeouts in the generator short" | Every Night Scanner exchange uses a 100 ms probe deadline, bounded by the same cancellation-token= and within the 300 ms Modbus deadline. Learner reads keep 300 ms. The capture note states the 100 ms value. | With the default plan, 8 sweep requests get no reply. At 300 ms that adds 2.4 s to every start and to every property case; at 100 ms it adds 0.8 s. Loopback replies arrive in about 1 ms, so 100 ms leaves a wide margin. | | A timeout must be real, not scripted | An entry is `timeout` only when the generator's deadline expired **and** the simulator recorder reports `Sent == null` for that connection. Any disagreement fails startup. | The log status is evidence from both ends of the exchange, not a constant. | | "Exactly one correct answer" must not come from script constants | `Diagnosis.AnswerEntry` derives the scanning client from the log (the only client addressing ≥ 3 distinct unit IDs) and takes its first entry. The generator checks that this equals the plan. | The verified rule depends only on evidence, like Phantom Writer's "values read from log entries". | | A property "for any seed" vs. a deterministic production log | `NightScannerPlan.Default` is fixed. `NightScannerPlan.FromSeed(seed)` derives a plan for tests from a SplitMix64 sequence. Both go through the same generator and validation. | Production stays deterministic (Req. 2.8); the property covers many plans. | | Hints are case-specific | Hints, task text and the flag label move to an additive `incident` object in `GET /api/scenarios`. | Avoids hard-coding scenario IDs in `app.js` and keeps Phantom Writer's text unchanged. | | Answer redaction could hint at the answer | ~~Keep Phantom Writer's rule: redact `log_entry.client` only when the submitted transaction is the answer entry.~~ Revised after the session 10 security review: the redaction and the "client label differs" wording marked the answer row (an answer oracle against Req. 3.6). Every unverified answer in both security cases now gets one identical reply with `log_entry: null`; only the echoed `answer` differs. Progressive hints stay client-side and generic. | The reply must not depend on which part of the pair was wrong. The harness checks this byte for byte for every log entry of both cases. | | A step deadline can expire during connect or write | `CaptureAsync` catches step-deadline cancellation around connect and write and rethrows `InvalidOperationException` naming the step and its deadline. The "5 s startup deadline" message is kept only for cancellation of the outer token. | The startup error names the real cause. | Out of scope: writes of any kind in the Night Scanner, Modbus gateway exception codes 0A/0B (the simulator stays silent, as documented in `modbus-protocol.md`), multiple scans per capture, sub-second timestamps. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph "Startup (before HTTP)" P[NightScannerPlan.Default] --> B[NightScannerScript.Build] B -- "IncidentStep[] (FC03 only)" --> C[IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync] C -- "loopback TCP, 100 ms per request" --> G[(Private gateway simulator
unit 5 + unit U, read-only)] G -- "recorder: received / sent bytes" --> C C --> V[Night Scanner validation
+ Diagnosis.AnswerEntry] V --> L[TrafficLog night-scanner] end L --> T[TrainingService] T --> LG[(Learner-facing gateway simulator
same device map, read-only)] UI[app.js] -- "GET /api/incident/night-scanner/log
POST /api/incident/answer
POST /api/test" --> T ``` Startup: the `TrainingService` constructor creates the troubleshooting simulators, generates the Phantom Writer log, then the Night Scanner log, all under one 5 s deadline, then creates the learner-facing `night-scanner` gateway simulator. The private gateway is disposed when `GenerateNightScannerAsync` returns. `GhostWireHost.Create` already resolves `TrainingService` eagerly, so a failure stops startup. ## Components and Interfaces ### `ModbusSimulator` (changed, `Modbus.cs`) ```csharp public ModbusSimulator(int unit, Dictionary> registers, bool allowWrites = false, IExchangeRecorder? recorder = null) : this(new Dictionary>> { [unit] = registers }, allowWrites, recorder) { } public ModbusSimulator(Dictionary>> devices, bool allowWrites = false, IExchangeRecorder? recorder = null); ``` `ServeAsync` looks up `devices[header[6]]`. A missing unit is recorded with `Sent = null` and kept silent, exactly as the single-unit mismatch today. All other request handling is unchanged. ### `IncidentStep`, `TrafficLogEntry` (changed, `Incident.cs`) ```csharp public sealed record IncidentStep(string Client, ushort TransactionId, int OffsetSeconds, byte Function, ushort Address, ushort QuantityOrValue, byte Unit = IncidentScript.Unit); public sealed record TrafficLogEntry(..., string status, IReadOnlyList frames, int? exception_code = null); ``` ### `IncidentLogGenerator.CaptureAsync` (extracted) ```csharp private static async Task> CaptureAsync(ModbusSimulator simulator, Recorder recorder, IReadOnlyList script, DateTimeOffset start, TimeSpan stepDeadline, CancellationToken= step, strictly in order: open a new `TcpClient` to `IPAddress.Loopback` and the simulator's port, remember the local port, write the encoded request, then read the 7-byte header and PDU and wait for end of stream under `stepDeadline`. After all steps, wait (bounded by `ct`, at most 1 s) until the recorder holds one exchange per step, then match exchanges to steps by remote port **and** transaction ID (script transaction IDs must be unique). Scan request k (k = 0 … N−1) at `ScanStartSeconds + k`, unit k+1, transaction `ScanFirstTransactionId + k`. Merged by time, HMI first on ties. All steps are FC03, quantity 1. Default plan, as inputs (the log values are whatever the simulator returns): scan of units 1–10 at 03:12:07–03:12:16 by `ENG-WS-13`, transactions 301–310; HMI polls at 03:12:00, :05, :10, :15, :20, transactions 1–5; 15 entries in total. `Devices(plan)`: `{ 5: { 3: { 100: 650 } }, U: { 3: { 0: RespondingValue } } }`. ### `IncidentLogGenerator.GenerateNightScannerAsync` (new) ```csharp public static Task GenerateNightScannerAsync(NightScannerPlan plan, CancellationToken= Validate the plan; build the script. 2.
